mechanism_narrative: A low and stable unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which positively impacts consumer confidence and spending, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE is below 4% but SPX returns are negative in more than 40% of the next 20 trading days, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) crosses above 4.5%, it indicates monetary tightening, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS remains above 4.5% but SPX returns are positive in more than 50% of the next 20 trading days, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both GDP (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) show concurrent growth, it signals strong economic demand, which drives corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If both GDPC1 and HOUST show growth but SPX returns are negative in more than 30% of the next 60 trading days, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) during a late-cycle expansion signals strong supply-side activity, which supports equity valuations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO growth is positive but SPX returns are negative in more than 40% of the next 60 trading days, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A high and rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) signals inflationary pressures, which may lead to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL growth exceeds 3% YoY but SPX returns are positive in more than 50% of the next 20 trading days, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals strong labor market conditions, which supports consumer spending and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.2% MoM but SPX returns are negative in more than 30% of the next 5 trading days, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) show concurrent growth, it signals strong demand, which drives corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If both RSAFS and HOUST show growth but SPX returns are negative in more than 30% of the next 20 trading days, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) during a monetary easing cycle signals lower borrowing costs, which supports equity valuations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS declines but SPX returns are negative in more than 40% of the next 60 trading days, this hypothesis is rejected.
